title: RingedRefinementAssembly
statement: For normalized ringed operations on the ordinary or vertical small pro-etale sites, the canonical ring direct-image compositor is given by the site fibre-product associator. A proper refinement triangle with open legs has its explicit clopen pullback shape. Its three geometric factors form a natural transformation and hence a canonical adjunct refinement. If the pre-mate geometric h-square, coefficient cocycle, open coefficient equations, refinement composition, identity and spatial coefficient equations hold (ElementaryCoherences), then all Laws hold: the remaining refinement coefficient square follows by the counit-transpose calculation, naturality follows from the natural transformation, and commuting coefficient squares follow from the coefficient cocycle. The scalar universal right Kan extension constructs coherent scalar shifts compatible with its cochain counit. The clopen projection commutes with shifts: its image equation makes it a natural retraction of the open counit, and such a retraction is unique. The inverse-scalar comparison field of ElementaryShifts implies Shifts for the canonical refinements: the localized exact open adjunction and normalized inverse-transpose equations first give shifts of beta and delta, pullback/open composition gives shifts of h, taking the coefficient mate preserves shifts, the refinement is its geometric unit followed by the direct image of h, and both coefficient-square composites are compositions of shift-compatible transformations with explicit associators. These laws and shift data assemble to Package m T.

source.place: 6.7.6–6.7.7, compactification independence; agent ordinary-derived ring-sheaf coefficient supplement to the clopen-section refinement construction, not a theorem literally asserted in the paper.

proof.text: Define canonicalCoefficients by sheafPushforwardContinuousComp applied to the inverse siteTriangle. Its section equation is definitional. For a proper refinement, take the scheme pullback, give it the Over T structure through its first projection, and define both arrows and the distinguished section using Over.homMk. Reflection by Over.forget proves the Over pullback condition. The properOpenSectionProperties theorem supplies the section retraction, clopenness and openness; the other projection equation is pullback.lift_fst.

Compose beta.hom, the two whiskered pi/sectionPull transformations, and openFactor.hom. Their components are definitionally the prescribed h maps. Whisker the geometric unit by the second open extension and compose with the direct image of this h transformation. This defines canonicalRefinements and its adjunct equation is definitional.

For the generic mate square, apply the inverse B-adjunction Hom equivalence injectively. Naturality in the target moves the B-direct image of delta1 outside the transpose; naturality in the source moves S(rA) outside. The mate counit equation replaces the remaining transpose by alpha followed by S of the A-counit. Naturality of alpha moves rA through it. Functoriality combines the A-adjunction transpose and its counit into hA, by the Hom-equivalence inverse law. The assumed h-square is now exactly the desired equality. Apply this calculation using r.adjunct at A and B to prove Laws.square.

The localized exact open adjunction commutes with shifts: pull its unit back along Q, express it through the termwise unit and the exact-functor factorization isomorphisms, and apply CommShift.of_whiskerLeft using essential surjectivity of Q. Pullback compositors, the identity compositor and the section/retraction comparison inherit shifts by exact localization. For any two shift-compatible adjunctions and a shift-compatible restriction square, the specified inverse-transpose equation uniquely identifies the inverse open comparison with the adjunct of a composite of the unit and restriction square. This generic adjunction calculation proves that comparison commutes with shifts. Specialize it to beta_inverse and delta_inverse. The unique-left-adjoint formula proves shifts of openFactor. Finally insert unitors and associators into the three factors of h, and use composition and whiskering to prove h commutes with shifts. None of beta, delta or h is a remaining shift hypothesis.

Apply rightKanExtension_coherentShift to the scalar cochain universal pair, whose left-derived property supplies its right Kan universal property. This fixes each shift comparison uniquely by its counit equation and supplies zero and addition coherence. canonicalScalarShifts chooses precisely this universally determined structure, and canonicalScalarCounit is the theorem's compatibility conclusion. Thus neither scalar shifts nor their counit compatibility is a remaining obligation.

The K-injective comparison identifies the right derived functor with the inverse of the K-injective localization equivalence followed by the termwise functor. Its transported shift structure makes that comparison shift-compatible. Naturality of the derived unit and the equivalence triangle equation identify its restriction to K-injectives with a composite of this comparison and the equivalence unit. K-injective resolutions detect the shift equation, since localization inverts their augmentations. Thus the right-derived unit commutes with shifts. The formula for the exact-left/right-derived adjunction unit, pulled back along Qh, is a composite of the termwise adjunction unit, this right-derived unit and the exact-left factorization. Its shift equation descends along the essentially surjective Qh. This proves geometric adjunction compatibility for the fixed standard shift structures, with no extra assumption.

For natural transformations ε:P→H and r,s:H→P with εr=εs=id, where H is full, apply naturality of rε to a preimage of sε. This gives rε=sε, hence r=s after composing with either retraction. For a shift-compatible ε:P→Id and a natural retraction r, both the shift of r and its conjugate by the shift comparison retract the shifted ε; fullness of the shift functor makes them equal. For the clopen pi, naturality of the open counit and pi_image give counit≫pi=id by the left triangle. Thus pi commutes with shifts without any complementary-open or equality-detection hypothesis.

Using the preceding derived open-comparison shift lemmas, install the universally constructed canonicalScalarShifts. The coefficient chi is a mate of the shift-compatible inverse-scalar comparison under shift-compatible geometric adjunctions. For the canonical refinement insert the right unitor and associator into its defining unit formula; the unit, h and whiskered composition commute with shifts. Insert the three necessary associators into the left coefficient-square composite and apply the composition and whiskering instances. The right composite follows directly. This constructs all four remaining Shifts fields without further assumptions.

Laws.natural is naturality of the actual left composite. Expand successive: the assumed coefficient cocycle rewrites its three comparison factors to the direct chi after the balanced hom; its leading balanced inverse cancels. Rewrite both successive maps in coefficient_square this way and substitute the equality between coefficient composites; both equality transports are then identities. Copy the remaining eight coherence fields. Finally assemble Package from these Laws, the given Shifts, the explicitly constructed refinements and canonicalShape at every refinement triangle.

proof_origin.place: The construction steps of the ordinary-derived coefficient supplement to 6.7.6--6.7.7, including the counit-transpose square and the formal transfer of elementary shift compatibility to mates and coefficient-square composites.
